leaves.label: Bhimbetka Rock Paintings
leaves.defn: Painted rock shelters of the Vindhyan hills from the Mesolithic to the historical period (UNESCO 2003): hunting scenes, dancers, Zoo Rock.
rows: Bhimbetka and Central Indian rock shelters

leaves.label: Petroglyphs of the Mongolian Altai
leaves.defn: The rock carvings and paintings of the Mongolian Altai (UNESCO 2011), from about 11,000 years ago to the Turkic period: Tsagaan Salaa, Upper Tsagaan Gol, Aral Tolgoi.
leaves.aliases: Petroglyphic Complexes of the Mongolian Altai

leaves.label: Tamgaly Petroglyphs
leaves.defn: The Bronze Age to medieval rock carvings of Tamgaly and the Semirechye (UNESCO 2004), with sun-headed figures and sacrificial scenes: sun-headed deities, bull and chariot scenes.

leaves.label: Maros-Pangkep Cave Art
leaves.defn: Painted and stencilled rock art of the limestone karst of South Sulawesi, among the oldest figurative art known (45,000+ years): Leang Tedongnge warty pig, Leang Bulu' Sipong 4 hunting scene, hand stencils.

leaves.label: Sangkulirang-Mangkalihat Rock Art
leaves.defn: Hand stencils and animal paintings of the limestone caves of East Kalimantan and of Niah in Sarawak: Lubang Jeriji Saléh banteng, Niah Painted Cave.

leaves.label: Zuojiang Huashan Rock Art
leaves.defn: Red-ochre rock paintings of the Luo Yue people on cliffs along the Zuojiang river in Guangxi (5th c. BCE–2nd c. CE), with figures and bronze drums (UNESCO 2016).

leaves.label: Bangudae Petroglyphs
leaves.defn: Neolithic and Bronze Age petroglyphs on the Daegok stream in Ulsan, with whales, hunters and boats, and the nearby Cheonjeon-ri carvings (UNESCO 2025).

leaves.label: Fugoppe Cave
leaves.defn: Incised figures and signs in the Fugoppe cave in Hokkaido (Epi-Jōmon) and the related Temiya cave carvings.

leaves.label: Helan Mountains Petroglyphs
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs pecked on the cliffs of the Helan and Yin mountains of Ningxia and Inner Mongolia, from the Neolithic to the medieval period: masks, animals and hunters (Helankou, Damaidi).
rows: Helan, Yinshan and northern Chinese petroglyphs

leaves.label: Saharan Rock Art
leaves.defn: Engraved and painted rock art of the Sahara from the Holocene to historical times, by stylistic phases: Bubaline engravings, Round Head paintings, Bovidian (pastoral) paintings, Dabous giraffes.
rows: Saharan rock art (Tassili, Acacus, Messak, Ennedi, Aïr)
Gilf Kebir and Uweinat (Eastern Sahara) rock art

leaves.label: San Rock Art
leaves.defn: Painted and engraved rock art of the San (Bushmen) of southern Africa, over tens of thousands of years: Drakensberg eland paintings, Twyfelfontein engravings, Tsodilo paintings.

leaves.label: Sasanian Rock Reliefs
leaves.defn: Royal reliefs carved on cliff faces in Fars and western Iran by the Sasanian kings, 3rd–7th century, following Achaemenid precedent: Naqsh-e Rostam investitures, Bishapur triumph of Shapur I, Taq-e Bostan.
rows: Sasanian rock relief (Rag-i-Bibi); route resolved: Sasanian rock relief at Rag-i Bibi (Q2127181)
row exemplar Fath-Ali Shah relief (Cheshmeh-Ali); see Islamic slice

leaves.label: Hittite Rock Reliefs
leaves.defn: Reliefs of gods and kings carved on rock in Hittite Anatolia, 14th–13th century BC: Yazılıkaya, Fraktin, Hanyeri, Taşçı.

leaves.label: Gobustan Rock Art
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of hunters, dancers, animals and reed boats pecked into the rocks of Gobustan in Azerbaijan from the late Upper Palaeolithic onward (UNESCO 2007).

leaves.label: Rock Art in the Hail Region
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of humans, animals and inscriptions at Jubbah and Shuwaymis in the Ha'il region of Saudi Arabia, spanning some 10,000 years (UNESCO 2015).
leaves.aliases: Hail rock art;Jubbah and Shuwaymis petroglyphs
rows: Arabian rock art (Ha'il, Shuwaymis, Bir Hima, Wadi Rum)
row exemplar Bir Hima Rock Petroglyphs and Inscriptions

leaves.label: Cueva de las Manos
leaves.defn: Stencilled hands and hunting scenes of guanacos painted in the Río Pinturas caves of Patagonia from c. 9300 BP (UNESCO 1999).
leaves.see: L1-17 Serra da Capivara Rock Art
rows: Patagonian rock art (Cueva de las Manos, Río Pinturas)

leaves.label: Serra da Capivara Rock Art
leaves.defn: The painted rock shelters of Serra da Capivara (Piauí), with Nordeste-tradition hunting, dancing and sexual scenes (UNESCO 1991): Pedra Furada, Toca do Boqueirão.
leaves.see: L1-16 Cueva de las Manos;L1-19 Chiribiquete Rock Paintings
rows: Serra da Capivara and Brazilian Nordeste rock art

leaves.label: Toro Muerto Petroglyphs
leaves.defn: Thousands of petroglyphs pecked on volcanic boulders at Toro Muerto (Arequipa) with dancers, camelids and birds, with related Andean sites: Toro Muerto, Toquepala Caves, Miculla.
rows: Andean rock art (Toro Muerto, Chile's Norte Grande)

leaves.label: Chiribiquete Rock Paintings
leaves.defn: Red-ochre paintings of jaguars, hunters and dancers on the tepuis of Chiribiquete in the Colombian Amazon (UNESCO 2018).
leaves.see: L1-17 Serra da Capivara Rock Art
rows: Amazonian and Orinoco petroglyphs (Chiribiquete, Monte Alegre)

leaves.label: Pecos River Style
leaves.defn: Large polychrome pictographs of shamanic figures painted in the rock shelters of the Lower Pecos Canyonlands of Texas and Coahuila (c. 2700 BCE onward): White Shaman Shelter, Fate Bell Shelter, Panther Cave.
rows: Lower Pecos rock art: Fate Bell Shelter, Seminole Canyon

leaves.label: Barrier Canyon Style
leaves.defn: Archaic pictographs of tall tapering ghost-like figures on the Colorado Plateau of Utah: Great Gallery, Horseshoe Canyon, Sego Canyon.

leaves.label: Chumash Rock Painting
leaves.defn: Polychrome pictographs of circles, wheels and beings painted in caves of the Chumash territory of southern California (c. 1000–1800): Painted Cave, Painted Rock (Carrizo Plain), Burro Flats.

leaves.label: Coso Rock Art
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of bighorn sheep, hunters and patterned-body figures in the Coso Range of the Mojave Desert, the largest concentration in North America.

leaves.label: Writing-on-Stone Rock Art
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs and pictographs of the Plains, incised in the sandstone of the Milk River valley, Alberta, including biographic warrior scenes (Áísínai'pi, UNESCO 2019).
rows: Plains and Rocky Mountain rock art (Writing-on-Stone)
La Barge Bluffs (Wyoming) is a second exemplar

leaves.label: Rock Paintings of the Sierra de San Francisco
leaves.defn: The Great Murals of Baja California: life-size red and black human and animal figures painted in the rock shelters of the Sierra de San Francisco and Sierra de Guadalupe (UNESCO 1993).

leaves.label: Arnhem Land Rock Art
leaves.defn: The painted rock shelters of the western Arnhem Land plateau and Kakadu, from Dynamic figures to the recent x-ray and contact paintings: Ubirr, Burrungkuy (Nourlangie), Nanguluwur, Injalak Hill.
rows: Arnhem Land and Kakadu rock art
row Arnhem Land and Kakadu rock art
row Arnhem Land and Kakadu rock art
row Arnhem Land and Kakadu rock art

leaves.label: Gwion Gwion Rock Paintings
leaves.defn: The fine-line figure paintings of the north-west Kimberley, slender tasselled human figures of great age.
rows: Kimberley rock art (Gwion Gwion / Bradshaw, Wanjina)

leaves.label: Murujuga Rock Art
leaves.defn: The petroglyphs of the Burrup Peninsula and Dampier Archipelago (Murujuga), over a million engravings made across tens of thousands of years.

leaves.label: Sydney Rock Engravings
leaves.defn: The outline engravings on Hawkesbury sandstone in the Sydney basin: animals, ancestral beings and people: Ku-ring-gai Chase sites.

leaves.label: Quinkan Rock Art
leaves.defn: The painted shelters around Laura on Cape York with the Quinkan spirit figures.

leaves.label: Panaramitee Style
leaves.defn: The widespread Australian engraving style of tracks, circles and dots ('track and circle'), among the oldest rock art of the continent: Ewaninga, Panaramitee.

leaves.label: Māori Rock Art
leaves.defn: The charcoal and red-ochre drawings in limestone shelters of South Canterbury and North Otago: Takiroa, Awamoko.

leaves.label: Franco-Cantabrian Cave Art
leaves.defn: Upper Palaeolithic painted and engraved cave art of south-western France and northern Spain, c. 40,000–11,000 BP: Chauvet, Lascaux, Altamira, Font-de-Gaume.

leaves.label: Côa Valley and Siega Verde Rock Art
leaves.defn: Open-air Upper Palaeolithic engravings of animals on schist outcrops in the Côa valley (Portugal) and at Siega Verde (Spain), c. 25,000–10,000 BP: Canada do Inferno, Penascosa, Ribeira de Piscos.
rows: Côa / Siega Verde open-air Palaeolithic rock art

leaves.label: Levantine Rock Art
leaves.defn: Post-Palaeolithic naturalistic rock painting of eastern Spain, c. 8000–3500 BC, with hunting, warfare and gathering scenes in shelters: Cova dels Cavalls, Roca dels Moros (Cogul), Valltorta.
leaves.aliases: Rock Art of the Mediterranean Basin on the Iberian Peninsula;Levantine art
rows: Levantine rock art (Mediterranean Basin of Iberia)

leaves.label: Iberian Schematic Art
leaves.defn: Schematic rock painting and engraving of the Iberian peninsula, c. 5000–1000 BC, associated with the first farming and metal-using cultures: anthropomorphs and idols, Galician petroglyphs of Os Mouchos and Portela da Laxe.

leaves.label: Cup and Ring Marks
leaves.defn: Neolithic and Bronze Age carvings of cups and concentric rings on outcrops and standing stones of Atlantic Europe, above all Britain and Ireland: Cochno Stone, Achnabreck, Roughting Linn.

leaves.label: Rock Carvings in Tanum
leaves.defn: Bronze Age rock carvings of Bohuslän in western Sweden, c. 1700–500 BC, with ships, warriors, ploughing scenes and weddings: Vitlycke panel, Aspeberget, Fossum.
rows: Tanum / Bohuslän Bronze Age rock carvings

leaves.label: Rock Carvings at Alta
leaves.defn: Rock carvings of hunter-fisher communities at Alta in Finnmark, c. 5000 BC – AD 0, with reindeer, elk, boats and bear hunts: Hjemmeluft, Bergbukten, Amtmannsnes.

leaves.label: Petroglyphs of Lake Onega and the White Sea
leaves.defn: Neolithic petroglyphs of Russian Karelia, c. 4000–2000 BC, on the shores of Lake Onega (swans, solar signs, the 'demon') and at Zalavruga on the White Sea (hunting and boat scenes).

leaves.label: Ural Pictograms
leaves.defn: Red-ochre rock paintings (pisanitsy) on river cliffs of the Urals, Neolithic to Iron Age, with animals, figures and signs: Ignatievskaya Cave, Tagil pisanitsa.

leaves.label: Rock Drawings in Valcamonica
leaves.defn: Petroglyphs of the Camunni in the Val Camonica (Lombardy), from the Epipalaeolithic to the Iron Age and beyond: Bedolina Map, Camunian rose, Naquane.

leaves.label: Umayyad Wall Painting
leaves.defn: the figural wall paintings of the Umayyad desert palaces, above all the bath of Qusayr 'Amra (8th century).

leaves.label: Persian Wall Painting
leaves.defn: the palace murals of Safavid and Qajar Iran (Chehel Sotoun, Ali Qapu, Hasht Behesht).

leaves.label: Al-Qatt Al-Asiri
leaves.defn: the geometric wall decoration painted by women inside the houses of the Asir region of Saudi Arabia (UNESCO 2017).

leaves.label: Ajanta Paintings
leaves.defn: Buddhist cave murals of Ajanta (2nd century BCE–5th century CE), the classical model for Indian wall painting: Padmapani, Mahajanaka Jataka.
rows: 19th-c. copies by John Griffiths and Bombay School of Art students
Early Indian cave-temple murals (Bagh, Ellora, Badami, Sittanavasal)
seam: classical cave murals beyond Ajanta

leaves.label: Sigiriya Frescoes
leaves.defn: The 5th-century paintings of women on the rock face of Kashyapa's palace at Sigiriya.

leaves.label: Kerala Mural Painting
leaves.defn: Temple and palace murals of Kerala (9th–19th century) in five colours: Mattancherry Palace Ramayana, Padmanabhapuram murals.

leaves.label: Kandyan Period Painting
leaves.defn: Buddhist temple murals of the Kandyan kingdom (1592–1815) in red and yellow narrative registers: Dambulla cave paintings, Degaldoruwa jatakas.

leaves.label: Shekhawati Frescoes
leaves.defn: Painted havelis, temples and forts of Shekhawati in Rajasthan, 18th–20th century, mixing Rajput, colonial and popular imagery.

leaves.label: Pithora Painting
leaves.defn: Ritual wall paintings of horses and deities by the Rathwa and Bhil of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.

leaves.label: Saura Painting
leaves.defn: Ritual wall paintings (ittal) of the Sora of Odisha dedicated to Idital.

leaves.label: Sohrai and Khovar Painting
leaves.defn: Harvest (sohrai) and marriage-chamber (khovar) wall paintings of Hazaribagh, Jharkhand.

leaves.label: Rangoli
leaves.defn: Ritual floor drawing in powder and rice paste across South Asia: kolam, alpana, kalamezhuthu.

leaves.label: Tibetan Buddhist Wall Paintings
leaves.defn: The secco murals of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries and temples across the Himalaya, from the Kashmiri-style programmes of Tabo and Alchi to Shalu, the Gyantse Kumbum and Guge: Alchi Sumtsek, Tabo assembly hall, Shalu murals.
rows: Western Himalayan Buddhist murals (Alchi, Tabo, Guge)
Newar murals strain the label; see problems
Western Himalayan murals row exemplar Q2705908
Western Himalayan murals row exemplar Q1112486
Tibetan Buddhist wall painting row exemplar Q25681

leaves.label: Dunhuang Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist cave temples of the Mogao Caves at Dunhuang (4th–14th century): Cave 217 Pure Land, Jataka narratives, donor portraits.

leaves.label: Kizil Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Buddhist caves of the kingdom of Kucha (Kizil, Kumtura and neighbouring sites), 4th–8th century, in rhomboid narrative grids and lapis blue: Cave of the Sixteen Sword-Bearers, Buddha in Nirvana.

leaves.label: Bezeklik Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Uyghur Buddhist caves of Bezeklik and the Turfan oasis (Qocho) under the Uyghur kingdom (9th–13th century): pranidhi scenes, Uyghur donor princes.
leaves.aliases: Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves murals;Uyghur Buddhist wall painting

leaves.label: Sogdian Wall Painting
leaves.defn: The secular and religious murals of Sogdian houses, temples and palaces (5th–8th century) at Panjikent, Afrasiyab and Varakhsha: Rustam cycle, Hall of the Ambassadors, Red Hall of Varakhsha.
rows: Sogdian and Bactrian wall painting (Panjakent, Afrasiyab, Bamiyan)
in situ row exemplar Q630805 / Q101467421
in situ row label (Bactrian, not Sogdian)

leaves.label: Bagan Murals
leaves.defn: The tempera wall paintings of the temples of Bagan (11th–13th century) and their Inwa and Konbaung successors: Abeyadana, Lokahteikpan Jatakas, Ananda temple.

leaves.label: Thai Mural Painting
leaves.defn: Tempera wall paintings of Thai Buddhist ordination halls and viharas, late Ayutthaya to early Rattanakosin and Lanna: Wat Phra Kaew Ramakien, Wat Pho, Wat Phumin, Wat Chong Nonsi.
rows: Wat Phumin and Wat Luang Wiang Ta Mon exemplars

leaves.label: Yongle Palace Murals
leaves.defn: The Daoist murals of the Yongle Palace in Shanxi (14th century), with the procession of deities in the Hall of Three Purities, and the Buddhist murals of the Fahai Temple near Beijing (1443).
rows: Chinese Buddhist and Daoist temple murals (Yongle Palace, Fahai)

leaves.label: Takamatsuzuka Tomb Murals
leaves.defn: Painted plaster walls of the late 7th-century tombs of Asuka (Takamatsuzuka and Kitora), with court ladies, the Four Directional Animals and star charts.
rows: Japanese tomb and temple wall painting (Takamatsuzuka, Kitora, Hōryū-ji)

leaves.label: Goguryeo Tomb Murals
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Goguryeo tombs near Pyongyang and Ji'an (4th–7th century): hunting scenes, dancers and the Four Guardians (UNESCO 2004).

leaves.label: Dancheong
leaves.defn: Korean polychrome painting of wooden buildings, temples and palaces in blue, red, yellow, white and black patterns; masters designated dancheongjang.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Church Painting
leaves.defn: Wall painting of Ethiopian churches, on plaster and on canvas glued to walls: Debre Berhan Selassie ceiling of winged faces, Lake Tana monastery murals, Lalibela paintings.
rows: Ethiopian church wall painting (Gondarine, Lake Tana)
row Ethiopian church wall painting exemplars

leaves.label: Litema
leaves.defn: Incised and painted mud-wall decoration of Basotho homesteads in Lesotho and the Free State, renewed by women.
rows: Litema and Sotho / Ndebele house painting

leaves.label: Ndebele House Painting
leaves.defn: Geometric mural painting of the Southern Ndebele of South Africa on homestead walls, by women (Esther Mahlangu).

leaves.label: Imigongo
leaves.defn: Rwandan relief panels of cow dung in black, white and red spirals and zigzags, from house walls to boards.
rows: row QID is Imigongo; agaseke is its own leaf

leaves.label: Egyptian Tomb Painting
leaves.defn: Wall painting in the tombs and temples of pharaonic Egypt, in tempera on plaster: Meidum Geese, Tomb of Nebamun, Tomb of Nefertari, Theban nobles' tombs.
rows: excluded row Egyptian, Thebes; Tomb of Nebamun

leaves.label: Minoan Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Fresco painting of Bronze Age Crete and the Minoanised Aegean, c. 1700–1450 BC: Bull-Leaping Fresco from Knossos, Akrotiri Spring Fresco, Fisherman of Thera.
leaves.aliases: Minoan frescoes;Aegean wall painting;Wall Paintings of Thera
rows: Aegean Bronze Age wall painting (Thera, Knossos)

leaves.label: Etruscan Tomb Painting
leaves.defn: Painted chamber tombs of Etruria, 7th–2nd century BC, chiefly at Tarquinia and Cerveteri: Tomb of the Leopards, Tomb of the Triclinium, François Tomb at Vulci.

leaves.label: Ancient Greek Painting
leaves.defn: Surviving Greek wall painting, mostly from tombs of the 5th–3rd century BC in Macedonia, Thrace and Magna Graecia: Tomb of Philip II at Vergina, Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak, Tomb of the Diver at Paestum.
rows: Macedonian and Thracian tomb painting (Vergina, Kazanlak, Sveshtari)
row exemplar Tomb of Philip II

Byzantine Empire, Ottoman Empire, Roman Republic, Kingdom of Pergamon, Roman Empire, Ptolemaic Kingdom, Seljuk Empire, Achaemenid Empire, Turkey, Seleucid Empire

leaves.label: Pompeian Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Roman wall painting of the Vesuvian cities and Rome, classed by August Mau in four Pompeian Styles, 2nd century BC – AD 79: Villa of the Mysteries, Villa of Poppaea at Oplontis, House of the Vettii.
rows: row label Pompeian Styles I-IV; Villa of the Mysteries

leaves.label: Catacomb Painting
leaves.defn: Early Christian and Jewish funerary and devotional wall painting of the 2nd–5th century, above all in the catacombs of Rome and at Dura-Europos: Catacomb of Priscilla, Via Latina catacomb, Dura-Europos synagogue.
rows: Roman and late-antique wall painting (catacombs, provincial)
Dura-Europos wall painting at Yale: Roman Syria; route resolved: Dura-Europos wall paintings at Yale; the leaf definition names Dura-Europos

leaves.label: Byzantine Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Fresco programmes of Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches, 6th–15th century: Cappadocian rock-cut churches, painted churches of Troödos, Panselinos at the Protaton, Mystras.
rows: Mount Athos and Late Byzantine Macedonian school (Panselinos)

Byzantine Wall Painting (L55), kind Russian 17th c. (Yaroslavl)

leaves.label: Faras Wall Paintings
leaves.defn: Wall paintings of the cathedral of Faras in the Nubian kingdom of Makuria, 8th–14th century, removed in 1961–64 to Warsaw and Khartoum: Bishop Petros with St Peter, Saint Anne, Nativity.

leaves.label: Maya Mural Painting
leaves.defn: The wall paintings of the Maya from the Preclassic to the Postclassic: San Bartolo murals, Bonampak Room 2 battle, Calakmul market murals.

leaves.label: Teotihuacan Mural Painting
leaves.defn: The fresco painting of the apartment compounds of Teotihuacan (c. 200–650 CE): Tepantitla Great Goddess, Tetitla, Atetelco.

leaves.label: Cacaxtla Murals
leaves.defn: The Epiclassic murals of Cacaxtla (Tlaxcala, c. 650–900 CE), mixing Maya and central Mexican styles: Battle Mural, Bird Man.
leaves.see: L2-36 Maya Mural Painting;L2-37 Teotihuacan Mural Painting

leaves.label: Moche Murals
leaves.defn: Painted and modelled mud-plaster friezes of Moche temples: Huaca de la Luna Ai Apaec friezes, El Brujo.

leaves.label: Mexican Muralism
leaves.defn: The public mural movement of post-revolutionary Mexico (1920s–1970s) led by Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros: Rivera's National Palace murals, Orozco's Hospicio Cabañas, Siqueiros' Polyforum.
leaves.see: L2-41 Chilean Muralism;L2-42 Murals of Revolutionary Nicaragua

leaves.label: Chilean Muralism
leaves.defn: Chilean public mural painting from the 1940s, from Siqueiros' Chillán murals to the brigade painting of the Brigada Ramona Parra.

leaves.label: Murals of Revolutionary Nicaragua
leaves.defn: Public murals painted in Sandinista Nicaragua (1979–1990) by Nicaraguan and international brigades.

leaves.label: Romanesque Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Fresco programmes of Romanesque churches, c. 1000–1200: Sant Climent de Taüll, Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, San Isidoro, León, Sant'Angelo in Formis.
rows: Spanish Romanesque frescoes in US museums; route resolved: Spanish Romanesque frescoes in US museums

leaves.label: Gothic Wall Painting
leaves.defn: Wall painting in Gothic churches and palaces, 13th–15th century, north of the Alps and in the Adriatic: Albi Cathedral, Saint-Sernin, Beram and Hrastovlje Danse macabre, Albertus Pictor's Swedish churches.
rows: Nordic church wall painting (kalkmålningar, Albertus Pictor)
Istrian and Slovene Gothic frescoes (Beram, Hrastovlje)

leaves.label: Painted Churches of Northern Moldavia
leaves.defn: The 15th–16th-century churches of Bukovina painted inside and out with Byzantine-derived cycles under Stephen the Great and Petru Rareș: Voroneț Last Judgement, Humor, Sucevița, Moldovița.

leaves.label: Scottish Renaissance Painted Ceilings
leaves.defn: Tempera-painted timber ceilings of Scottish houses and castles, c. 1550–1650, with emblems, grotesques and heraldry: Prestongrange, Aberdour Castle, Culross Palace.

leaves.label: Murals in Northern Ireland
leaves.defn: Loyalist and republican political murals painted on gable walls in Northern Ireland since the early 20th century and above all from the 1970s: Falls Road murals, Bogside Artists, King Billy murals.

leaves.label: Samchyky Painting
leaves.defn: The decorative painting of the walls and interiors of houses in Samchyky village (Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine), with unique floral patterns.

leaves.label: Illusionistic Ceiling Painting
leaves.defn: Ceiling and vault painting in fresco that opens the architecture to a painted sky by foreshortening (di sotto in sù) and painted architecture (quadratura), from Mantegna to the Baroque and Rococo: Mantegna's Camera degli Sposi oculus, Pietro da Cortona's Barberini ceiling, Pozzo's Sant'Ignazio, Tiepolo's Würzburg staircase.
leaves.aliases: quadratura;di sotto in sù;sotto in su;Baroque ceiling painting

leaves.label: Italian Renaissance Fresco
leaves.defn: The fresco cycles painted on the walls and vaults of Italian chapels, churches and palaces from Giotto to the High Renaissance, studied where they stand: Arena (Scrovegni) Chapel, Brancacci Chapel, Sistine Chapel ceiling, Raphael Rooms.
leaves.see: A5-20 Italian Renaissance Painting;A5-16 Gothic Painting;B2-9-44 Gothic Wall Painting;L2-49 Illusionistic Ceiling Painting

leaves.label: Umayyad Mosaics
leaves.defn: the glass wall mosaics of the Dome of the Rock and the Great Mosque of Damascus (7th–8th century), made by Byzantine-trained craftsmen.
rows: Umayyad mosaics (Dome of the Rock, Great Mosque of Damascus)

leaves.label: Zellige
leaves.defn: geometric mosaic of hand-cut glazed tiles set in plaster, the wall and floor revetment of Morocco and al-Andalus.
leaves.see: E1-10 Fez Pottery. Possession taxonomy: Zellige (C8 Building Materials & Hardware).

leaves.label: Moʿaraq (Cut-Tile Mosaic)
leaves.defn: the tile revetment of Iranian and Central Asian architecture: cut-tile mosaic (mo'arraq) of the Timurid and Safavid periods, haft-rangi (seven-colour) tiles and banna'i brick-and-tile.
leaves.see: E2-2 Kashan Lustreware; L3-4 Kashi Kari.

leaves.label: Kashi Kari
leaves.defn: the tile-mosaic revetment of Mughal and Punjabi buildings (Lahore, Multan, Thatta).
rows: kashigari of Multan; vessels as well as revetment, see problems

leaves.label: Aina-kari
leaves.defn: mirror mosaic: cut mirror glass set in plaster on walls and ceilings of Iranian palaces and shrines.

leaves.label: Hellenistic Mosaics
leaves.defn: Greek floor mosaics from the 5th to the 1st century BC, from pebble mosaics to tessellated opus vermiculatum: Pella stag hunt, Alexander Mosaic, Sosos's unswept floor.

leaves.label: Roman Mosaics
leaves.defn: Floor and wall mosaics of the Roman world, 1st century BC – 5th century AD, with strong regional schools in North Africa, Antioch and Sicily: Nile mosaic of Palestrina, Antioch mosaics, Villa Romana del Casale, Bardo mosaics.
leaves.see: L3-6;L3-8. Possession taxonomy: Mosaic tile (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Mosaic nippers (C4 Craft & Art Supplies).
rows: Roman mosaics of the East (Antioch, Zeugma)

leaves.label: Byzantine Mosaics
leaves.defn: Glass and stone wall mosaics of Byzantine churches and of the workshops they trained, 5th–14th century: San Vitale, Ravenna, Hagia Sophia, Daphni and Hosios Loukas, Monreale, San Marco.
rows: Middle Byzantine mosaics (Hagia Sophia, Hosios Loukas, Daphni, Nea Moni)
Early Christian and medieval mosaics of Rome

leaves.label: Azulejo
leaves.defn: Painted tin-glazed tile panels covering walls of churches, palaces and streets in Portugal, Spain and Brazil from the 16th century: Palace of the Marquises of Fronteira, São Bento station, Valencian ceramic retables.
leaves.see: E1-8 Hispano-Moresque Ware;A6-19-2 Zellige. Possession taxonomy: Azulejo (C8 Building Materials & Hardware).

leaves.label: Trencadís
leaves.defn: Mosaic of broken tile and crockery shards laid on curved surfaces, the cladding of Catalan Modernisme (Gaudí, Jujol): Park Güell, Casa Batlló, Hospital de Sant Pau.

leaves.label: Portuguese Pavement
leaves.defn: Patterned pavement of black basalt and white limestone setts laid by hand in Portugal and its former colonies since the 19th century: Rossio waves, Copacabana promenade.

leaves.label: Soviet Mosaics
leaves.defn: Monumental mosaics on public buildings, metro stations and housing of the Soviet Union and its republics, 1920s–1991, a state programme of monumental art: Kyiv and Donetsk school mosaics, Yerevan facade mosaics.

leaves.label: Steppe Geoglyphs
leaves.defn: The earthen and stone ground figures of the Turgai Trough in northern Kazakhstan (Neolithic–Iron Age), at least 260 squares, rings and crosses: Ushtogay Square, Turgay triradial swastika.

leaves.label: Gozan no Okuribi
leaves.defn: The five bonfire characters and figures (Daimonji, Myōhō, the boat and the torii) lit on the hills around Kyoto on 16 August, laid out as fixed hillside figures.

leaves.label: Nazca Lines
leaves.defn: Geoglyphs scraped into the desert of the Nazca and Palpa pampas (c. 500 BCE–500 CE), with straight lines and animal figures (UNESCO 1994): Hummingbird, Monkey, Condor, Palpa figures.

leaves.label: Pintados Geoglyphs
leaves.defn: Hillside geoglyphs of the Atacama made by removing or piling stones (c. 600–1500 CE): Cerro Pintados panels, Atacama Giant, Chug-Chug.

leaves.label: Acre Geoglyphs
leaves.defn: Geometric ditched enclosures of the south-western Amazon (Acre, Brazil), c. 0–1300 CE.

leaves.label: Effigy Mounds
leaves.defn: Earthen mounds raised in the shapes of animals and serpents in the Eastern Woodlands: Serpent Mound, the bear and bird mounds of Effigy Mounds National Monument.

leaves.label: Blythe Intaglios
leaves.defn: Giant human and animal figures scraped into the desert pavement near Blythe on the lower Colorado River.
rows: North American intaglios and effigy figures (Blythe)
bucket also holds Serpent Mound (kind of L62) and Newark Earthworks (K11 earthwork)

leaves.label: Hill Figures
leaves.defn: Figures cut into hillsides to expose the chalk or limestone beneath, mainly in southern England, from the Bronze Age (Uffington) to the 18th–19th-century white horses: Uffington White Horse, Cerne Abbas Giant, Long Man of Wilmington.

leaves.label: Deq
leaves.defn: the facial and hand tattooing of Kurdish, Arab and Amazigh women.

leaves.label: Godna
leaves.defn: Tattooing of the tribal communities of central and eastern India (Baiga, Gond, Oraon), also transferred to painting on paper.

leaves.label: Mehndi
leaves.defn: Henna body painting of South Asia for weddings and festivals.

leaves.label: Sak Yant
leaves.defn: Thai, Khmer, Lao and Burmese protective yantra tattooing of sacred diagrams and Khom script, applied by monks and ajarn with a steel rod.
rows: Mainland and Indonesian SE Asian tattooing (sak yant, Mentawai, Chin)

leaves.label: Mentawai Tattooing
leaves.defn: The full-body line tattooing (titi) of the Mentawai of Siberut, west of Sumatra.

leaves.label: Batok
leaves.defn: The traditional tattooing of the Philippines, from the Visayan pintados to the Kalinga and Bontoc warrior tattoos.

leaves.label: Irezumi
leaves.defn: Japanese tattooing, above all the Edo-period full-body designs inspired by ukiyo-e heroes, with the Okinawan women's hand tattoos (hajichi) and Ainu lip tattoos as kinds.
rows: Irezumi and Japanese tattooing (incl. hajichi, Ainu)

leaves.label: African Scarification
leaves.defn: Cicatrisation and keloid scarification as body art across Africa, with named regional marks: Yoruba facial marks (ila), Nuba and Dinka marks.
rows: row African scarification: Yoruba tribal marks (Q25080696)

leaves.label: Kakiniit
leaves.defn: Inuit women's facial and body tattooing, sewn or pricked with soot-blackened sinew, revived in Nunavut and Greenland since the 2000s.

leaves.label: Tā Moko
leaves.defn: Māori tattooing, chiselled (uhi) into the skin in curvilinear designs that mark descent and rank: moko on men's faces, moko kauae for women.

leaves.label: Polynesian Tattooing
leaves.defn: The tattoo traditions of Polynesia worked with toothed combs and a mallet: Samoan peʻa and malu, Marquesan full-body tattoo, Tahitian tatau, Fijian veiqia.
rows: Polynesian tatau (Samoa, Tahiti, Marquesas, Hawai'i, Tonga, Fiji)

leaves.label: Sailor Tattoos
leaves.defn: The Western tattoo tradition of sailors and its prison and street derivatives, which grew into the American traditional style of bold outlines and limited colour (Sailor Jerry): swallows, anchors, pin-ups.
rows: Western sailor, prison and modern tattooing

leaves.label: Sona
leaves.defn: Sand drawings (lusona, pl. sona) of the Chokwe and neighbouring peoples of eastern Angola: continuous lines around a grid of dots, illustrating stories.

leaves.label: Navajo Sandpainting
leaves.defn: Dry paintings of coloured sands, pollen and charcoal made by Diné medicine men for healing chants and erased after use, and their permanent versions glued on board for sale since the 1930s.

leaves.label: Corpus Christi Flower Carpets
leaves.defn: Carpets of flowers laid on the streets of Polish villages (Spycimierz and others) for the Corpus Christi processions (UNESCO 2021).
leaves.aliases: Flower carpets tradition for Corpus Christi processions
rows: Flower carpets tradition for Corpus Christi processions
